extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar).
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.citeAs: Rohatgi, S., Qin, Y., Aw, B., Unnithan, N., & Kan, M.-Y. (2023). The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics. arXiv:2305.14996v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Crawling PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, followed by full-text extraction and enhancement using Semantic Scholar's API to fetch additional information such as citations and external links.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Full-text extraction fails mostly for papers between the years 2000 to 2015. Specific missing data includes: 19 sections not detected in a sample of 21 papers; 25 footnotes missing out of 92; 28.78% of figures not detected; 31.58% of tables not detected and 46.06% detected with wrong contents or titles.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Removed PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Full-text extraction using GROBID in S2ORC-JSON format. Extraction of figures and tables using PDFFigures. Linking with the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) via Graph API. Language detection using a public language detection toolkit. Topic prediction using a PLM-based supervised method (SPECTER).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Topic labels were generated using a pre-trained language model (SPECTER) trained on a subset of 2,545 scientific papers with ground truth topic labels scraped from conference websites. The model predictions are integrated as silver-labeled topic information.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Model-predicted topics are silver data. Two works in 'Resource & Evaluation' were incorrectly predicted due to insufficient training samples and high overlap with other topics. Accuracy on top-cited papers (87%) is higher than the test set (69%) mainly because of the bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID, PDFFigures, BART-large-MNLI, SciBERT, SPECTER, Language detection toolkit
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which papers recently added to the ACL Anthology are downloaded and processed by monitoring changes in URLs. The maintainers plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Accelerates scientific progress and promotes reproducibility in research by providing accessible and standardized data resources. Highlights the need for attention on emerging topics like 'Ethics of NLP' and declining underrepresented topics like 'Discourse and Pragmatics' and 'Phonology, Morphology and Word Segmentation'.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics (e.g., Machine Translation). Linguistic disparity: numerous languages remain underrepresented, and there is a significant disparity in coverage even among languages in the same language group. The corpus is limited to peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Small-scale collection focusing only on peer-reviewed, open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology (not comprehensive like S2ORC). Limitations of GROBID in formatting information extraction (figures, tables, equations). Unlabeled resource lacking annotations for specific tasks. Full-text extraction failures mostly for papers between 2000 and 2015.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Temporal topic trend analysis, document-level information extraction, section-wise tasks (e.g., related work generation), fine-grained linguistic analyses, multimodal research (e.g., figure caption generation), emerging topic detection, evolution detection of topics, paper-reviewer matching, document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific LLMs, fine-tuning general LLMs, building scientific assistants, summarization, contribution extraction, future work prediction, analysis of generalization ability of NLP models, examining modifications in pre-prints, historical language change analysis, construction of knowledge graphs.
